correctness.rationale: Exact root-support reductions (6)--(7) are verified by exhaustive comparisons. The joint two-sided Gaussian rare-event process converges to independent spatial Poisson processes using Mills ratio and multinomial Poisson convergence. Explicit high/low mark truncation justifies the noncompact ordered argmax and time-gap mapping. The global extremal pair belongs to exactly one order orientation, so the limiting loss is strictly positive. The split-sample inequality (10) and uniform Gaussian extreme-value moments prove expected-loss convergence. The Gaussian radius is independent of spherical direction, validating intrinsic normalization. The conditional Poisson void formula (11) establishes the exact expectation representation. The included checker passes 900 finite exact support trials and 45 independent truncated-Poisson brute-force checks; those tests corroborate, not prove, the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The result determines a natural high-dimensional Euclidean invariant and a nontrivial universal width-loss distribution for every transitive tournament, with an exact mean coefficient and a macroscopic law for the normal-cone exposed vertex. The contrast is intrinsic: a previously known outer sphere is supported only by n-1 short roots, whereas almost every random direction exposes a macroscopically long root and the total angular weight of sphere contacts tends to zero. This separates metric boundary contact from normal-cone concentration and is not a tiny finite numerical improvement or arbitrary parameter slice.
